title: Screenshot design review
summary: A collection of nouns and verbs for reviewing a user interface screenshot against design rules: a screenshot sent with little or no text described first, captures at named widths and themes, text size, contrast, cropping, overflow, alignment, spacing and broken assets measured from each capture's layout, every failing check recorded as a finding with its capture and location, a proposed fix verb for each, and a re-render at the same widths and themes verified by a different worker.
boundaries: Findings, fixes and closing use the findings to fixes pack; this pack adds intake, captures and measured checks.
Captures use local or test pages with synthetic data; a screenshot that shows personal data is never recorded.
A matter of taste is a palette brief, never a finding.
No verb changes the page; importing the pack writes nothing and enqueues nothing.

nouns.title: A collection of nouns and verbs for reviewing a user interface screenshot against design rules

value.lets_workers: Review a user interface screenshot against design rules: describe a screenshot sent with little or no text before judging it, capture the page at named widths and themes, measure text size, contrast, cropping, overflow, alignment, spacing and broken assets from each capture's layout, record every failing check as a finding with its capture and location, propose a fix verb for each, and have a different worker re-render the same widths and themes and verify every fix.

flow.when: Triage confirms each finding's kind and severity.
A taste call gets a palette brief instead of a fix.
In a local copy, with a page check that fails first.
A different worker, at the same widths and themes.

complements: Findings, fixes, verifications and closing come from the findings to fixes pack; this pack adds the screenshot-first intake, the capture matrix and the measured design checks.
The contrast formula is visual and 3D rendering's worked example, pinned rather than redefined.
Captures use the video and motion pack's Playwright and Chromium tool cards; a matter of taste becomes a taste palettes brief.
value.worked_example: Synthetic: a phone screenshot with no text, described first; a volunteer sign-up page captured at 320, 768 and 1440 CSS pixels in light and dark; 29 failing checks across all seven rules, recorded as seven findings with their cells and boxes; and a re-render that verifies the contrast fix and finds the alignment fix still failing at 1440.

nouns.title: Guardrail: describe a screenshot before judging it
nouns.category_reason: A guardrail is a reusable rule every verb in this work follows, with the check that proves it.

value.rule: Say what a screenshot shows before judging it: the page and state as far as they can be seen, the visible text exactly, the apparent theme and how it was told. Mark what cannot be seen as unknown, such as the width in CSS pixels, the build and the address. Concerns stay observations until a capture measures them.
value.how_it_is_checked: A screenshot description lists visible text, unknowns and proposed captures, and records no finding.

nouns.title: Guardrail: every finding names its capture and location
nouns.category_reason: A guardrail is a reusable rule every verb in this work follows, with the check that proves it.

value.rule: Every finding names each capture cell it was seen in by width and theme, the screenshot's digest, the element's selector and box in CSS pixels, the rule it breaks, what was measured and the threshold.
value.how_it_is_checked: The design finding checks fail any finding without a located screenshot and a measurement.

nouns.title: Guardrail: a fix is verified at the same widths and themes
nouns.category_reason: A guardrail is a reusable rule every verb in this work follows, with the check that proves it.

value.rule: A fix is verified by re-rendering every cell of the original capture plan on the fixed build and rerunning every check. A fix seen at one width or theme is not verified at the others, and a new failure anywhere is a new finding.
value.how_it_is_checked: A verification lists the fixed build's screenshots for every cell the finding failed in, and fix_verified needs all of them to pass.

nouns.title: Capturing a page at named widths, themes and states
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call deterministic procedure: the same inputs always give the same result.

rules: Capture every cell: each width with each theme and each state the request names. 320 CSS pixels is where WCAG's reflow rule applies.
Use a pinned browser build through the pinned Playwright version, set the theme with its color scheme emulation, and set reduced motion to reduce.
Take full-page screenshots with animations disabled, the text caret hidden and one image pixel per CSS pixel.
Wait for fonts and network to settle before each capture; record a failed cell with its reason instead of retrying silently.
Collect each cell's layout facts from the same render: every text element's box, font size, weight and colors; every control's clipping; every image's load state; the document's scroll width.
Store every screenshot and layout by SHA-256. Use test pages and synthetic accounts only; never capture personal data.

nouns.title: Design rules measured from a capture's layout
nouns.category_reason: A fixed set of checks with thresholds and methods that every capture is scored against.

checks.fails_when: Any text element's computed font size is below min_text_px.
checks.basis: A team default of 12 CSS px; WCAG sets no minimum size, so the request may set another.

checks.fails_when: Text contrast is below 4.5:1, or below 3:1 for large text: at least 24 CSS px, or at least 18.66 CSS px and weight 700.
checks.basis: WCAG 2.2 success criterion 1.4.3, with relative luminance computed as in visual and 3D rendering's contrast example.

checks.fails_when: An element that hides its overflow holds content more than 1 CSS px wider than its box.
checks.basis: WCAG 2.2 asks for no loss of content when text is resized or respaced (1.4.4, 1.4.12).

checks.fails_when: The document's scroll width is above the viewport width, so the page scrolls sideways.
checks.basis: WCAG 2.2 success criterion 1.4.10, reflow at 320 CSS px.

checks.fails_when: A member of a declared alignment group sits 1 CSS px or more off the group's most common edge.
checks.basis: The groups the request declares; nothing is guessed from the picture.

checks.fails_when: A gap between consecutive members of a declared stack is not a multiple of spacing_unit_px.
checks.basis: A team default spacing scale of 4 CSS px.

checks.fails_when: An image did not load or has a natural width of 0.
checks.basis: The browser's own load state for each image.

rules: Reproduce the contrast example's expected ratios before checking anything; stop with blocked if they differ.
Every check reports its measurement and threshold; a check that cannot run is not_run with a reason, never a pass.
passed is true only when no check fails in any cell.

Every cell and rule appears once in counts.

nouns.title: Checklist a person runs before trusting a design review
nouns.category_reason: A short checklist a person runs is part of the review's guardrails.

items: A screenshot sent without words was described before anything was judged.

nouns.title: Design finding checks, with the worked example's findings and bad ones the validator recomputes
nouns.category_reason: A golden fixture: fixed findings and the recorded results of every check.

value.purpose: Deterministic checks every finding this pack records passes on top of the findings to fixes record checks, each shown failing on a bad finding for exactly its own reason. The seven good findings are the worked example's.

deterministic_checks.why: A broken design rule is a design flaw in the findings to fixes pack's terms.
A visual finding comes with the screenshots it was seen in.
Each screenshot names its capture cell and the element's box in CSS pixels.
The finding states the rule, what was measured and the threshold.
Every piece of evidence names where it was seen, at which widths and themes, and its digest.
Duplicates fold together by page, rule and element.
A newly recorded finding is open; only triage and close move it on.
A matter of taste is a palette brief, not a finding.
Captures use synthetic or test data only; a screenshot that shows personal data is never recorded.
Every finding carries its proposed fix verb.

verbs.title: Describe what a screenshot shows, before judging it
verbs.summary: Describe a screenshot sent with little or no text: what page and state it seems to show, the visible text exactly, the apparent theme and how it was told, what cannot be known from it, the likely concerns as observations, and the capture cells that would measure them.
verbs.outcome: A screenshot description; no finding yet.

slots.name: screenshots
slots.description: Pins of the nouns holding the screenshots the person sent, stored by SHA-256.

slots.name: review_request
slots.description: Pin of the review request, if one exists.

steps: Say what is visible before saying what is wrong, and transcribe visible text exactly, cut-off words included.
Mark the width in CSS pixels, the device scale, the address, the build and the state unknown unless the screenshot shows them.
Stop with blocked when the screenshot shows personal data, and ask for a capture with a synthetic account.
Keep concerns as observations and propose plan-captures; a reaction of taste goes in taste_reactions, for a palette brief.

acceptance.check: The output validates against template.screenshot-description's schema.
css_width is null with an unknown unless the screenshot states the width.
proposed_cells covers every default width with every default theme.
The description says only what the screenshot shows.

verbs.title: Plan every capture cell and its settings
verbs.summary: Turn the review request into a capture plan: every width with every theme and state, the pinned browser, the viewport and device scale, and the settings that make captures repeatable.

slots.name: screenshot_description
slots.description: Pin of the screenshot description, if the review started from one.

steps: List every width with every theme and every state the request names, once each.
Use the capture matrix's settings unless the request names others, and say why when it does.

acceptance.check: The output validates against template.capture-plan's schema.
cells holds each requested width, theme and state exactly once.

verbs.title: Capture every cell's screenshot and layout
verbs.summary: Render the page once per cell of the capture plan with the pinned browser, take a full-page screenshot, collect the cell's layout facts from the same render, and store both by SHA-256.
verbs.outcome: A capture set and the layout facts of every cell.
network: Only the page address the capture plan names, a local build or a test page with synthetic data, read without signing in; no other hosts, and browser downloads only under the worker's own policy.
steps: Capture every cell with the plan's settings; record a failed cell with its reason.
Collect layout facts from the same render as the screenshot, never from another load.
Stop with blocked when a page shows personal data or needs a real account.

acceptance.check: The output validates against template.capture-set's schema.
Every plan cell appears once in the capture set and once in the layout facts.
Each capture's layout_facts_sha256 is the digest of that cell's layout facts.

verbs.title: Measure every design rule in every cell
verbs.summary: Reproduce the contrast example, then apply the seven design rules (text size, contrast, cropping, overflow, alignment, spacing and broken assets) to every cell's layout facts, recording each check's measurement and threshold.
steps: Reproduce the contrast example's expected ratios first; stop with blocked if they differ.
Apply every rule to every cell with the request's thresholds, groups and stacks; never guess a group from the picture.
Set passed only when no check fails in any cell.

acceptance.check: The output validates against template.design-check-report's schema.
Every cell and rule appears once in counts.
Recomputing the rules from the pinned layout facts reproduces the report exactly.

verbs.title: Record each failing rule as a located finding
verbs.summary: Record one finding per rule and element that failed, in the findings to fixes shape, with a screenshot for each cell it failed in, the element's box and the measurement, and propose a fix verb for each; a matter of taste becomes a palette brief instead.
verbs.outcome: Design findings, each with its proposed fix verb.

slots.name: check_report
slots.description: Pin of the design check report.

slots.name: screenshot_description
slots.description: Pin of the screenshot description, if the review started from one.

steps: Group failures by rule and element; record one open finding for each group, naming every cell it failed in.
Give each finding a screenshot item per cell with its box, and one measurement item with the rule, measurement and threshold.
Propose findings-to-fixes.triage and then findings-to-fixes.propose-fix for each finding, and list both in its work as pending.
Turn a taste reaction into a palette brief, never a finding; run both sets of record checks before submitting.

acceptance.check: Every finding validates against template.finding's schema.
Every finding passes the findings to fixes record checks and the design finding checks.
Every failure in the check report belongs to exactly one finding.

verbs.title: Re-render every cell and verify each fix (a different worker)
verbs.summary: A worker who wrote neither the fix nor its proposal re-renders every cell of the original capture plan on the fixed build, reruns every design check, and writes one verification per finding: fixed only when every cell it failed in now passes.
verbs.outcome: The fixed build's captures, layout and checks, and a verification for every finding.

slots.name: findings
slots.description: Pins of the findings the fix addresses.

slots.name: fix
slots.description: Pin of the fix, from the findings to fixes pack's fix verb.

slots.name: check_report
slots.description: Pin of the design check report from before the fix.

network: Only the page address the capture plan names, a local build or a test page with synthetic data, read without signing in; no other hosts, and browser downloads only under the worker's own policy.
steps: Confirm you wrote neither the fix nor its proposal; otherwise end blocked.
Re-render every cell of the original plan on the fixed build and rerun every check, not only the finding's cells.
Write fix_verified only when every cell a finding failed in now passes, and fix_failed when any still fails.
Propose record-design-findings for any new failure in any cell; never fix it inside this verb.

acceptance.check: The output validates against template.design-check-report's schema.
The new capture set holds exactly the original plan's cells.
Each verdict follows from the before and after failures of its finding's cells.
The verifying key differs from the keys that wrote the fix and its proposal.
